title: Call Out and Get Curious About a Team Members Improvement
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece distinguishes between praising a team member's improvement and naming it as a 'Statement of Progress,' which explicitly describes how someone has grown over time rather than just celebrating an outcome. It argues the real power comes from pairing that observation with curious follow-up questions that ask team members to explain their own progress, shifting the moment from external validation to internal discovery. Most professional development, the piece notes, is done to people through assigned training or coaching, which stops working the moment a leader's attention moves elsewhere. By contrast, a team member who can articulate what changed builds a portable, self-owned toolkit for future challenges.
